questions.subject: MATH
questions.learningObjective: Solve problems involving logic circuits and truth tables.
questions.stem: During a review of the topic, for a deeper check, solve the problem that follows: A combinational circuit has 8 binary inputs and one output. How many rows are in its truth table?
questions.explanation: With 8 binary inputs there are 2 to the power 8 distinct input combinations, so the truth table has 256 rows. Choice B is a distractor: it squares the input count. Choice C is a distractor: it doubles rather than exponentiates. Choice D is a distractor: it omits one input combination.
questions.hint: Each input doubles the number of rows.

provenance.author: bank-team-math-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MATH
questions.learningObjective: Solve problems involving logic circuits and truth tables.
questions.stem: For a take-home task, for a deeper check, solve the problem that follows: A circuit is built from 8 two-input AND gates, each fed by distinct external wires. How many external input wires are required?

options.misconception: it counts gates instead of their input wires
it adds two wires regardless of gate count

questions.explanation: Each of the 8 gates needs two input wires and no wires are shared, so the circuit requires 16 external inputs. Choice B is a distractor: it counts gates instead of their input wires. Choice C is a distractor: it squares the gate count. Choice D is a distractor: it adds two wires regardless of gate count.
questions.hint: Two input wires per gate, all distinct.

options.misconception: it uses a square grid sized by the variable count

Choice B is a distractor: it uses a square grid sized by the variable count. Choice C is a distractor: it allocates two cells per variable. Choice D is a distractor: it doubles the required cells.
questions.hint: One cell per possible input combination.

stimulus.body: In a discrete math review, consider the following question: A Boolean function of 6 variables is true on 18 assignments. How many cells of its Karnaugh map contain a zero?

questions.stem: In a guided example, for a deeper check, try this exercise: A Boolean function of 6 variables is true on 18 assignments. How many cells of its Karnaugh map contain a zero?

options.misconception: it counts the ones instead of the zeros
it counts every cell as zero
it adds one extra zero cell

questions.explanation: The Karnaugh map has 2 to the 6 cells, of which 18 hold ones, leaving 46 cells holding zeros. Choice B is a distractor: it counts the ones instead of the zeros. Choice C is a distractor: it counts every cell as zero. Choice D is a distractor: it adds one extra zero cell.
questions.hint: Subtract the one-cells from the total cell count.
